solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sailor, half frozen, stumped by subzero conditions

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

indicators.note: keeps the first half of the word

parts.note: the first half of FROZEN
st = stumped on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A sailor, half frozen, is beaten by the icy weather at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' is a cricket dismissal, abbreviated on the scorecard; 'by' just places it after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk figure who brings frost stands, by personification, for freezing weather itself.

clue.text: Judge in court keeping legatee's case cordial?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so up encloses the outer letters

parts.note: up, as in up before the magistrate, means appearing in court

indicators.note: a word's case is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the possessive belongs to the surface: the case is that of the word legatee

explanation.surface: A judge in court keeps an heir's will case friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'up' before a magistrate is to be in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A julep is a sweet drink, often a medicinal syrup, and a cordial is such a drink; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Smart chap holding hat raised is mark of a soft-spoken character

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something reads it upwards, reversing it
to hold is to clasp within, so the chap's name wraps around the hat

parts.note: a smart alec; Alec is a chap's name
lid = hat, informally

explanation.surface: A dapper man doffs his hat, the sign of someone gently spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'soft-spoken character' is a letter, not a person: the mark under a C tells you to say it soft, as in façade.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: the hook under ç tells you that character, the letter C, is pronounced soft.

clue.text: Playing with wind trio, flautist out of time

indicators.note: wind as a verb means twist about, so the letters are rearranged
out of shows that a letter is left out of the pooled letters before rearranging

explanation.surface: A flautist plays with a wind trio and loses the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like part of a wind trio; it is the verb to twist, the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone playing in the sense of toying or dallying romantically is being coquettish, teasing a would-be lover.

clue.text: Go too far with party in the wake of several balls

indicators.note: a wake is the trail behind a ship, so the party comes behind, after, the balls

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone overindulges at a party after a round of balls, or a bowling session.
explanation.walkthrough: The balls are cricket deliveries, six to a set, not dances.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to exaggerate or overindulge is to go beyond sensible limits.

clue.text: St Anton native perhaps has to limit year on slope

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on' puts a piece below, after, the rest

parts.note: the word itself
yr = year
a lean is a slope

explanation.surface: A local of the Austrian ski resort St Anton spends a year on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: St Anton am Arlberg is a ski resort in western Austria; 'perhaps' flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: St Anton lies in Austria's Tyrol region, so its natives are one kind of the answer.

clue.text: Putting down my name, sign for holiday place in Italy

parts.note: a sign of the zodiac
'my!' and 'cor!' are both exclamations of surprise; removed
n = name; removed

explanation.surface: Someone signs a form, writing their name, to book an Italian holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting down my name' reads as signing up; in fact it tells you to drop two pieces from the star sign. Cor is British slang for surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the island in the Bay of Naples is a classic Italian holiday destination.

clue.text: Socialist shortly gets up and leaves

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means rising, so the letters read from the bottom upwards
shortly means cut short, leaving just the abbreviation's first three letters

explanation.surface: A socialist quickly stands and walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: lettuce leaves. 'shortly' cuts Socialist to its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of lettuce with long crisp leaves, also called romaine.

clue.text: One may be found in bed, knocking back excellent fruitcake after workout

definitions.text: One may be found in bed

indicators.note: to knock back is to turn back

parts.note: PE = physical education, a workout

indicators.note: 'after' places the reversed piece behind the workout letters

parts.note: A1 = excellent, with the 1 read as I
a fruitcake, like a nut, is a crazy person

explanation.surface: Someone lounging in bed after the gym, downing a slab of fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed. A1, meaning first-rate, becomes AI as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition by example: this bedding plant is one of many flowers grown in garden beds.

clue.text: Cromwell's cavalry — mounted men breaking guts

indicators.note: to break into something is to force a way inside it, so RO goes into the guts

parts.note: insides = guts
OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Cromwell's horsemen hack their way through their enemies' bellies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted men' looks like it defines cavalry, but 'mounted' is the signal to turn the soldiers upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name: the nickname of Oliver Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War.

clue.text: One reluctant to change light in the kitchen is ringing friend endlessly

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the light word goes round the friend

parts.note: lite is the food-label spelling for low-fat or light products

indicators.note: endlessly means without its ends, the first and last letters

parts.note: a buddy is a friend

explanation.surface: A kitchen bulb seems to be calling a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims BUDDY to UDD, which LITE rings. 'light' suggests a lamp; it is the diet-food word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Luddite was originally a machine-breaking textile worker, now anyone who resists new technology.

clue.text: Heading west, sailor's leading series of races in Uruguay's River Plate

parts.note: río is Spanish for river, the language of Uruguay

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front

parts.note: OS = ordinary seaman; the 's is 'is'
the TT, the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races

explanation.surface: A sailor sails west to lead a regatta on the River Plate in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Plate' reads as one name, the estuary between Uruguay and Argentina; it splits, with the river in Spanish and Plate as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plate in the sense of a dish of food; this Italian rice dish is one, a definition by example.

clue.text: Edge chipped off delicate china

parts.note: pale = delicate, as in a pale pink; drop the final E

explanation.surface: A fragile piece of porcelain loses a chip from its rim.
explanation.walkthrough: China here is rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so china means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so china means friend.

clue.text: Game twin kids play without delay on a regular basis

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside
letters at play move about freely, so TWIN KIDS is rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, rearranged and split in two

indicators.note: take every other letter of DELAY

parts.note: the odd letters of DeLaY

explanation.surface: Twins play a game together without dawdling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, an old sense, so the rearranged twins wrap around the regular letters of delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: flicking small discs into a cup is one parlour game.

clue.text: Learner leaving two-barrelled shot gun in the outback?

definitions.note: in Australian slang a gun is a top performer, a champion

indicators.note: the learner is said to leave, so its letter is taken out of the pool of letters
shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, telling us the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A shooting scene: someone fires a double-barrelled shotgun after the novice has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of TWO-BARRELLED, remove one L ('Learner leaving'), and rearrange the rest ('shot'). 'Shot gun' looks like one shotgun, but 'shot' is the anagram signal and 'gun' begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians call an outstanding performer a gun, which is exactly what a champion who beats everyone is.

clue.text: One's skill in quiz crystal clear

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun: read it as 'clear crystal'

parts.note: the word itself
I = one, taken out of QUIZ
art = skill, put in its place

explanation.surface: A contestant's talent at a quiz makes the answers crystal clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's skill' means one is skill: I becomes ART. The phrase 'crystal clear' is then read backwards as a clear crystal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock crystal is the colourless, transparent form of this mineral: a clear crystal by definition.

clue.text: Squeeze in to tank having larger dimensions than normal

indicators.note: to tank is to collapse, so the letters fall apart

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone squeezing into a tank that is bigger than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is a phrase with nearly the same sound as its own answer, which makes it hard to see as an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the size label for beds and sheets bigger than a standard double.

clue.text: One keeps back shock career, not allowed to be spoken about

indicators.note: to be spoken about means the words are said aloud, giving soundalikes

parts.note: to career is to rush along, as does to hare; banned means not allowed

explanation.surface: A shocking career that nobody may mention.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, HARE sounds like HAIR and BANNED like BAND. 'shock' is a mass of hair, not a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairband holds a mop of hair away from the face, and a shock is a thick mass of it.

clue.text: Consume uranium in energy plant

indicators.note: 'in' puts the consuming and the uranium inside the energy, as fuel sits in a plant

parts.note: vim = energy
to burn fuel is to consume it
U, the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A nuclear power plant burning uranium to make energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to a power plant; the plant is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this genus of flowering shrubs, such as guelder rose, is a plant.

clue.text: Stick around outside public house, or I can be transported

indicators.note: outside places the reversed word round the other pieces
around signals the letters being turned back to front

parts.note: a cue is the stick used in snooker and pool
PH is the map abbreviation for public house, a pub

explanation.surface: Someone leaning on a stick outside a pub, or perhaps being carried home.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away by intense joy, overwhelmingly happy.

clue.text: One aiming to sell diamond surrounds this sportsman

definitions.meaning: the diamond is a baseball field; this player throws from its centre

explanation.surface: A jeweller tries to sell a diamond ring to an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: The diamond is a baseball field, not a gem; the mound stands at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who makes a sales pitch, and the baseball player throwing from the middle of the diamond.

clue.text: Fizzy drink overflowing in round dish

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the whole result is read backwards
overflowing means spilling round, so the drink surrounds the little word

parts.note: soda is a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: A soft drink spilling over into a round serving dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like the bowl in the picture, but it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adonis is a very handsome young man, and a dish is slang for an attractive person.

clue.text: Area right between west end of nave and entrance

definitions.text: Area right between west end of nave and entrance

indicators.note: between says the two short pieces sit with the nave's edge on one side and the spell on the other
west end of means the leftmost letter, the start of the word nave as written

parts.note: to entrance is to bewitch, and to hex is to put under a spell

explanation.surface: An architect's description of the porch space lying between a church's nave and its door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb, to bewitch, not a doorway. The whole clue also defines the answer: that space at the west end of the nave is exactly what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: In church architecture this is the porch or vestibule across the western end, before the nave proper.

clue.text: Moderate results from having booster jab study

indicators.note: to have is to hold, so the study holds the booster inside it

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room
an amp (amplifier) boosts sound

explanation.surface: Test results are muted because someone had a booster vaccination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booster jab' reads as one vaccine; only the booster matters, as the thing that boosts a guitar's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to moderate is to tone down or restrain.

clue.text: Nothing like a century to reverse form

indicators.note: AS A TON is written backwards

parts.note: as a ton: a ton is a hundred, a century
usage = customary form or practice

explanation.surface: A batter's form is nowhere near a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: A ton is a hundred, so 'like a century' is 'as a ton'. The answer is a British idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom meaning nothing at all, as in 'we got not a sausage'.

clue.text: It's time for stag do on river

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece 'on' another comes after it

parts.note: r = river
ut is the old name for do, the first note of the scale

explanation.surface: A stag party on a river boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The stag do is a pre-wedding party in the surface; here 'do' is the musical note and the stag is a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: the deer's mating season is the time when stags fight and breed.

clue.text: Totally casual kicks hampering tango

definitions.note: 'casual' marks the answer as informal slang for 'totally'

indicators.note: to hamper is to hem in, so the kicks surround the tango

parts.note: to toe a ball is to kick it
T is tango in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Casual trainers (kicks) get in the way of a tango dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicks' wants to be trainers; here it is a verb, and to toe is to kick.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent informal slang: a clipped form of 'totally', and 'casual' flags that register.

clue.text: Inches in front of drone — a new animal

indicators.note: to be in front of is to come first, so the inches lead the rest

parts.note: in = inches
a drone is a low hum
the word itself
n = new

explanation.surface: A drone inches forward toward a strange new creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' is an adjective here, meaning brutish, not a noun for a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: animal behaviour is brutish, lacking human feeling.

clue.text: Part of spring vegetable uprooted

indicators.note: pulled up, so read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: a yam is a root vegetable

explanation.surface: In spring, a gardener uproots a root vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' is the season, not a coil or a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the three months of the northern spring.

clue.text: Casual firing range warning?

definitions.meaning: a random shot taken without careful aim
a range is a kitchen stove; split the answer 3-4 with an apostrophe

explanation.surface: A warning notice at a rifle range about casual shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: The range is a kitchen stove, not a shooting range, so the warning is "pot's hot". The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a shot fired carelessly at random, and, split apart, the cook's warning that the pot is hot.

clue.text: Daughter leaving very much in advance

parts.note: as in 'love dearly'
d = daughter, removed

explanation.surface: A daughter leaves home, sadly and far too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very much' is as in 'I'd dearly love to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: before the expected time, ahead of schedule.

clue.text: Shorter of two chords from Iron Maiden hit is on American guitar

indicators.note: hit as in battered, so the letters are knocked about
in an across clue, one piece 'on' another comes after it, so IS follows the guitar

parts.note: IRON plus M, maiden in cricket
ax, US slang spelling of axe, a guitar
the word itself

explanation.surface: A song by the heavy metal band Iron Maiden, played on an American guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chords' and the guitar pull toward music; the chords are geometry, lines across an ellipse. M is a maiden over in cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometry term: of an ellipse's two principal chords through its centre, this is the shorter one.
